The treaty secured trade routes and stability between the two powers. The name 'Ettifaq', meaning 'concord' or 'agreement', is believed to have originated from this treaty.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that The Founding of the Shia Imami Ismaili State (1320 AD) The name Ettifaq carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: The term 'Ettifaq' was also used to refer to the administrative structure of the Ismaili state established by Imam Aga Khan I. 'Ettifaq' represented the high council or the supreme assembly of the Ismailis, which functioned as the central governing body of the state. This term highlights the importance of unity and common purpose within the Ismaili community.
